featured_reviews.name: Nitin Dhiman
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dear Sir/Madam,

This was my 8th regular service, and due to the nature of my work and travel, I have experienced automobile service centres in many parts of India. Sadly, the one consistent factor across most of them is the poor quality of customer experience combined with a complete lack of accountability.

My recent experience at NBS Mahindra International, Mumbai during my 70,000 km service is yet another example of this ongoing issue.

Let me clarify this very clearly at the outset:
My complaint is NOT against the technician working on my vehicle, nor the relationship manager assigned to me.
Both conducted themselves professionally and were doing their job.

The issue lies entirely with the supervising staff member
(Mr Yogesh Vaidya)
who was moving around the service floor, “bossing” the area and attempting to assert authority without any understanding of the actual situation.

Due to multiple past experiences of negligence and shortcuts (for example: rear drum assemblies not even being opened and yet being declared “OK”), I did not feel comfortable sitting in the lounge and blindly trusting the process. I chose to stand at a safe and reasonable distance from my car and quietly observe the work being carried out.

I am fully aware of service centre protocols. I am an adult who understands workshop environments, and I did not interrupt, instruct, or interfere with any technician.

Yet, the supervising staff member accused me of:
• Creating a disturbance
• “Setting up my home” in the service area
• Hindering the workflow

If that were actually true, I would not hesitate to apologize. But it was a baseless, unnecessary and disrespectful accusation targeted at a concerned, observant customer.

This behaviour is unacceptable.

I own a Toyota Fortuner and previously owned an Innova, and never in my ownership experience have I faced such hostility for simply wanting transparency and proper care of my vehicle. The difference in professionalism is stark.

It is deeply unfortunate that as someone who wants to support Indian automobile manufacturers, it is experiences like this that make me hesitant every time I consider choosing one.

This is not how a brand builds loyalty. It is how trust is destroyed.

I request the following:
1.	An internal inquiry into the behaviour of the supervising staff member present on the service floor at NBS Mahindra International, Mumbai on the day of my service.
2.	Clear instructions to supervisory staff on how to respectfully handle customers.
3.	Allowing customers to observe their own vehicles from a safe distance without being treated as an inconvenience.
4.	Accountability and corrective action, not excuses.

Once again, I repeat the technician and relationship manager were not the problem. The issue is with the senior, supervising individual who misused his position and authority.

I expect a formal response and clarification on the action being taken.

Regards,
Nitin Dhiman

featured_reviews.name: Mithun Sawant
featured_reviews.review_text: I visited this service center for my first service of Mahindra 3XO. Initially I was asked to wait for a while as there were 2 customers in line and I was offered tea/coffee which was a great gesture. After a long wait, I was aligned with a relationship manager. After discussing few things with him about the car I was asked to wait. I learned from him that for the first service they just wash the vehicle, check the engine oil & coolant, etc in all only 4-5 checks were supposed to ne done. I duly respect the lunch hours that the workers will take but atleast I should come to know about the current status and an approximate ETA of it’s completion. Even after asking them multiple times, I was given wrong information everytime and in all I waited for 4hrs just for my first service. Even though the service provided by the team was great but atleast I should know the truth. Eventually, I came to know that my vehicle was not even in queue and was just kept at a side. When I tried to escalate my case, they completed my vehicle quickly but it was done in so fast as to just deliver the vehicle. I understand that the workshop is very busy but atleast giving me the correct status of my vehicle would have helped. In all my first service was a bad experience as I almost wasted my half a day waiting at the workshop.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had given my old model Thar for servicing on Saturday, 1st November 2025, after being assured by the service representative, Mr. Tejas, that it would be ready by Monday ie 03 November 2025. However, today is Wednesday, and the vehicle is still not returned. What’s worse, there has been no proactive update from their side — I’ve had to call every day, only to receive a different excuse each time.

To add to the frustration, I even received a traffic challan on 5th November 2025 for the same vehicle — which, according to their own records, is still in their custody! When I informed Mr. Tejas, he said he’d check and revert, but, unsurprisingly, no one followed up.

This entire experience has been extremely disappointing and unprofessional. Such carelessness and lack of accountability reflect very poorly on their service standards. I would strongly advise others to think twice before trusting their vehicle with this service center.

featured_reviews.name: Vinod Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very disappointing service experience

I purchased a brand-new Mahindra XUV700 from NBS International Chowpatty in December 2024. Unfortunately, from day one the vehicle had starting issues and cluster display problems. My new car had to be sent to the Sewree service center, where it remained for 4–5 days before being returned after repairs.

After nearly a year, in the first week of February 2026, I visited the Sewree service center again for the second scheduled service. At that time, my car had no dents and no AC problems — only a slight sound during clutch movement. When I reached the service center, more than 25 cars were parked outside and there was barely any space inside. I was already concerned about leaving my vehicle given the overcrowded and poorly managed situation.

After the service, the clutch sound issue was addressed. However, upon delivery I discovered a dent on the rear side of my car, and the AC was not functioning properly — problems that did not exist before service. Even worse, my dash cam had been disconnected during servicing without my knowledge or consent.

I reported everything to the service center head and escalated the matter to the company as well, but no proper action has been taken so far.

Extremely poor handling, lack of accountability, and very disappointing after-sales service. Not the experience anyone expects after purchasing a new vehicle, from NBS INTERNATIONAL Mumbai.

When I confronted them then their answer was vague that I can book the service to Arnav Modi service centre which is 50 kms away ftom my residence. The NBS international at Sewri must be making money out of rescheduling the service to some anti social activities. The Mahindra Vehicle management must seek the clarification from their service centre if they want to sustain in the car market else Mahindra will have the same path like Ola EV scooters.
